name: Thumbnail Store
description: ThumbnailStore, the disk preview store: opaque encoded preview bytes (it never decodes images, and CoreAsset never imports CoreRaster) keyed by PreviewKey (asset, content token, SizeClass of 256, 1024 or 2560 px), each PreviewEntry naming its optional VolumeRef and relative path, and Availability (online, or offline with the volume). PreviewFiles is the layout: index.json, index.journal and p/<2 hex>/<16 hex>.bin files named by a 64-bit FNV-1a of the key, so no user text reaches a path; each file is FLPV, a version byte, a 4-byte big-endian length and that much JSON header naming its key, volume and path, then the payload. Every change runs under an exclusive flock on the folder's lock file and replaces a file by writing <name>.tmp whole, then renaming it over the old one. A write evicts the entry read longest ago (ties: the larger size class) while the payload bytes exceed the budget; opening a store never evicts. A read checks that the file's header names its key, returns nil and drops the entry when the file is gone, and bumps lastRead in memory; bumps are flushed with the next change, by the first read 2 s or more after the last flush, and on deinit, merged with the index on disk. PreviewJournal appends only the entries a change touched (FLPJ1:, the index's 16-hex generation, a newline, then one JSON put or drop per line); each store catches up on the lines others appended, ignores an unfinished last line and a journal of another generation, and compacts into a new snapshot past max(64, entries / 2) records, so index I/O per write is O(1) amortised. PreviewIndex is the snapshot codec (version 2; a version 1 index still loads) and its recovery: an index that fails to decode, names another version or an impossible size, or whose journal has a damaged line is renamed to index.damaged.json (its journal to index.damaged.journal, both kept) and rebuilt from the files: key, volume and path from each header, byteCount from the payload, lastRead from the modification date; a file whose header doesn't decode or that sits under another key's name is skipped and left on disk. Opening also deletes orphan .tmp files and drops entries whose file is gone. OfflineVolumes never probes the file system: the caller passes the mounted volume ids; entries(on:) matches by volume id alone, so a renamed volume keeps its entries; an entry whose volume id is not mounted reports offline while its bytes still read, and an entry with no volume is always online. Limits: the budget counts payloads only, not headers or the index; a negative budget throws; every failure is an AssetError; volume and duplicate facts beyond the entries belong to the catalog once its schema lands.
